newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks fail to recover in afternoon.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks fail to recover in afternoon.

text.p: Banking shares were mostly lower in Wednesday afternoon trade, unable to recover from rumours concerning Nippon Credit Bank Ltd which sent the sector reeling in the morning, brokers said.

At 0428 GMT, Nippon Credit was down 27 yen at 189 and was the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse with 13.588 million shares changing hands. It was followed by Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd, which shed 16 yen to 147 in trade of 5.383 million shares.
Fuji Bank Ltd, ranking sixth with 4.18 million shares traded, lost 50 yen to 1,280. Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd was down 20 yen at 1,820.
Industrial Bank of Japan fell 70 yen to 1,480 and Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LCTB) was down 30 yen at 430.
"The sell-off of bank shares ignited by selling of Nippon Credit Bank has spread even to banks like the Industrial Bank of Japan," a broker at a middle-sized brokerage said.

Stock market dealers said participants began to dump NCB's shares in the morning after Japanese government bond prices soared on vague talk that it would hold an emergency news conference. There was also a vague rumour about a possible merger involving NCB, they said.

An NCB official denied the rumours and after the market closed for the noon break, the bank said it saw no cause for concern about its financial health. It also said that it would take serious note of the stock market's view of its share price.
